newsitem.title: BOSNIA: First post-war Belgrade bus arrives in Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: First post-war Belgrade bus arrives in Sarajevo.

text.p: The first postwar coach from Belgrade arrived in Sarajevo on Monday, an early, concrete result of recently agreed diplomatic relations between Bosnia and Yugoslavia and a snub to recalcitrant Bosnian Serb leaders.
The bus, arriving two hours late and carrying 39 Serbian journalists and businessmen, was greeted with applause from waiting dignitaries.
The coach is expected to become a common sight in a city that was besieged for 43 months by Bosnian Serb forces backed by Belgrade which in 1993 broke off relations with its hardline proteges.

Yugoslavia and Bosnia agreed on October 3 in Paris to establish full diplomatic relations and increase trade and transport, establish a customs union and permit travel between the two countries without visas.
The Belgrade transport company Lasta and Sarajevo's Centrotrans signed a contract to enable their buses to shuttle between the cities on a daily basis from Wednesday.
The buses will cross former front lines in Bosnia, passing through Serb and Moslem-Croat territory.
But apparently expecting problems from hardline Bosnian Serb authorities in eastern Bosnia, the bus avoided the Serb stronghhold of Pale 16 km (10 miles) south of Sarajevo.
It travelled instead through north and central Bosnia via Bijeljina, Tuzla and Kladanj.

Bosnian Serb authorities, who have so far snubbed pressure by the world and Serbia to join Bosnia's governing bodies in line with the Dayton peace accord, have reacted angrily at the Yugoslav-Bosnian Paris agreement.
A Centrotrans official said that his company had already sold 30 tickets for Wednesday's first commercial trip.
Until now, Bosnians from the Moslem-Croat federation travelling to Belgrade have had to cross former front lines on foot and take a bus from the Serb half of the country.
The official said Centrotrans was working on setting up 18 more lines with other Serbian cities, some of them expected to be running by mid-November.
